title: Dividing by a Decimal
short: Multiply both numbers by 10 or 100 so the divisor is whole.
trouble: Children shift the decimal point in the divisor but not in the dividend.

blocks.html: You can divide a decimal by a whole number, and you know that multiplying by 10 shifts every digit. To divide by a decimal, turn the divisor into a whole number first.
Multiply the divisor and the dividend by the same power of 10, enough to make the divisor a whole number. The quotient does not change. Then divide: $4.8 \div 0.6 = 48 \div 6 = 8$.

Division asks how many times one amount fits in another. If both amounts get 10 times bigger, the answer stays the same: $6 \div 2 = 3$ and $60 \div 20 = 3$. In tenths: $4.8 \div 0.6$ asks how many 6 tenths fit in 48 tenths, which is the same as $48 \div 6$.

blocks.name: numberline
blocks.cap: Jumps of $0.6$ from 0 to $4.8$: eight jumps, so $4.8 \div 0.6 = 8$.

blocks.title: Write zeros in the dividend
steps: The divisor has 2 decimal places, so multiply both by 100.

blocks.html: Moving the point in the divisor only: $4.8 \div 0.6$ becomes $4.8 \div 6 = 0.8$. Multiplying just one number changes the problem. Check: dividing by a number less than 1 gives an answer bigger than the dividend, and $8 \times 0.6 = 4.8$ confirms 8.
